questions.stem: What does IP stand for in network protocols?
questions.explanation: IP stands for Internet Protocol, which is the principal communications protocol in the Internet protocol suite for routing packets.

questions.stem: Which network device operates at the physical layer and simply repeats signals to all ports?
questions.explanation: A hub is a basic network device that connects multiple computers but broadcasts all traffic to all ports, operating at the Physical Layer.

questions.stem: What is the standard port number for HTTP web traffic?
questions.explanation: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) traffic defaults to port 80, while secure HTTPS traffic defaults to port 443.

questions.stem: Which topology connects all devices to a single central cable?
questions.explanation: In a bus topology, all nodes are connected directly to a single transmission line or cable called a bus.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of a router?

options.A: To forward data packets between different networks
options.B: To connect local printers to a computer
options.C: To allocate power to network cables

questions.explanation: Routers operate at the Network Layer to connect different networks and route packets based on IP addresses.

questions.stem: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for end-to-end communication control, reliability, and flow control?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer (Layer 4) handles data transport reliability, error recovery, flow control, and multiplexing (e.g., TCP).

questions.stem: What is the main difference between TCP and UDP?

options.A: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable, while UDP is connectionless and faster
options.B: TCP operates at the physical layer, while UDP operates at the network layer
options.C: UDP is connection-oriented, while TCP is faster

questions.explanation: TCP ensures delivery using handshakes and confirmations, whereas UDP sends packets immediately without confirmation, making it faster but less reliable.

questions.stem: What protocol is used to automatically assign IP addresses to devices on a network?
questions.explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) dynamically assigns IP configurations to network hosts.

options.A: A unique physical address hardcoded into a network interface card
options.B: A temporary address assigned by an ISP
options.C: The software registration ID of macOS

questions.explanation: A MAC (Media Access Control) address is a unique, permanent hardware identifier assigned to network adapters.

questions.stem: Which wireless standard is commonly used for short-range personal area networks (PANs)?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless communication technology designed for PANs (connecting phones, headphones, mice, etc.).
